one_liner: Rust crypto crate with a ring-style API over AWS-LC and optional FIPS module; beat OpenSSL in wtx handshake runs.
what_it_does: A Rust library of crypto primitives (AEAD, digest, HMAC, HKDF, key agreement, signatures, RSA, RNG, plus extras such as unauthenticated AES modes, CMAC, AES key wrap and a post-quantum KEM module) whose API copies ring 0.16, so ring code mostly switches by changing the import. All crypto runs in AWS-LC, which the aws-lc-sys crate compiles from bundled C/assembly source (or aws-lc-fips-sys when the `fips` feature is on). It has no TLS or X.509 layer and no OpenSSL-compatible API: a TLS stack such as rustls or WTX sits on top, and rustls recommends its aws-lc-rs provider (it was rustls's default feature before 0.24).
how_it_is_fast: The wrapper adds no crypto of its own. The speed is AWS-LC's: BoringSSL-derived assembly (AVX-512 AES-GCM routines on x86_64), vendored s2n-bignum assembly for X25519, Ed25519 and P-384 scalar multiplication, and large precomputed elliptic-curve tables. Rust calls go over thin FFI into a statically linked, symbol-prefixed library, initialized once through std::sync::Once. In the wtx benchmark OpenSSL carries an almost constant 2-5 ms extra per run, which points to OpenSSL setup or integration overhead rather than faster primitives. Against ring the times are close (1.38 vs 1.29 ms at the fastest point), except with RSA-PSS certificates, where ring and Graviola win.
when_to_use: A Rust service that must use a FIPS-validated module: the `fips` feature links AWS-LC-FIPS 4.x (lab-tested and submitted to NIST) with the same API, and try_fips_mode() checks it at runtime.
rustls deployments that want post-quantum key exchange or the most complete provider: rustls recommends rustls-aws-lc-rs, and its ring provider has no post-quantum algorithms.
Porting ring 0.16/0.17 code that also needs AES-CBC/CTR, CMAC, AES key wrap or ML-KEM, which ring does not offer.
Handshake-heavy servers that use P-384 key agreement: in wtx it was fastest or near-fastest with secp384r1.
Mainstream targets (x86_64/aarch64 Linux, macOS, Windows) where a C compiler is available at build time.
when_not_to_use: no_std or embedded targets: the crate requires std.
Latency-critical handshakes with RSA-PSS certificates: in wtx aws-lc-rs took 6.4-6.7 ms, against 4.9-6.5 ms for ring and 5.2-5.9 ms for Graviola.

Size- or build-time-constrained builds: issue #745 (open) reports +4 MB (AWS SDK) up to +17 MB (MSVC static) and about 1.8 MiB more than ring on x86_64 Linux; a user reports builds several times slower than ring (#851). opt-level s/z (v1.18.0+) cuts the AWS-LC footprint 60-70% on x86_64, but P-256 becomes about 2-3x slower and P-384 about 3-6x slower.

Short-lived processes and cold starts: the guide gives a one-time jitter-entropy cost of about 50 ms per process, and #899 reports a ~1 s Lambda cold-start regression. AWS_LC_SYS_NO_JITTER_ENTROPY=1 removes it (non-FIPS only).

Old or unusual cross toolchains: #1022 (open) fails on aarch64 manylinux GCC 4.8.5 (no __ARM_ARCH), FIPS builds with GCC 14+ are still reported broken (#569), and Windows x86 needs NASM (x86-64 can opt into prebuilt NASM objects).

integration.dependencies: aws-lc-sys (bundled AWS-LC source built by a cc-crate build script; needs a C/C++ compiler, and NASM on Windows x86 unless prebuilt objects are allowed), zeroize, untrusted 0.7 (default ring-io/ring-sig-verify features). The `fips` feature swaps in aws-lc-fips-sys and always needs CMake and Go, plus bindgen/libclang except on 6 targets with pre-generated FIPS bindings.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.71 (rust-version) and a C11 compiler by default; a few tier-3 targets (mips, aarch64-apple-tvos-sim) need nightly.
integration.platforms: Built and tested on Linux (x86_64, aarch64, arm/armv7, i686, ppc/ppc64/ppc64le, riscv64gc, s390x, mips), macOS and iOS, Windows MSVC and GNU (x86, x86_64, aarch64), Android, FreeBSD, NetBSD, illumos and wasm32-emscripten. FIPS is a subset: Linux x86_64/aarch64/arm-musl/ppc, macOS x86_64/aarch64, Windows MSVC x86_64/aarch64, FreeBSD x86_64.
integration.thread_safety: Key types are Send + Sync (for example aead::LessSafeKey on docs.rs), and library init is guarded by std::sync::Once. There is no wider documented contract; the FIPS service indicator is thread-local.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it does not replace OpenSSL's API or libssl. It replaces ring 0.16 with documented differences (std required, extra check on Ed25519 PKCS#8 v2 keys), and as a rustls CryptoProvider it replaces OpenSSL only if you move the TLS layer to rustls.

gotchas: The build silently links a system AWS-LC if OPENSSL_DIR, OPENSSL_INCLUDE_DIR/OPENSSL_LIB_DIR or pkg-config points at a new-enough AWS-LC install. Dynamic linking embeds no rpath. Set AWS_LC_SYS_USE_SYSTEM=0 to force the vendored build, as the wtx benchmark did. With `fips`, detection may execute the candidate library.

FIPS is a compile-time Cargo feature. It unifies across the whole dependency graph, `fips` plus `non-fips` is a compile error, and the FIPS module version follows the crate version (module 3.0.x needs aws-lc-rs <1.18, 2.0.x needs <1.12), so pin the version to stay on a certified module. The FIPS static library is Linux/BSD x86_64/aarch64 only; other platforms get a shared library.
ML-KEM decapsulation (mlkem-native since aws-lc-sys 0.39) overflowed macOS's 544 KiB default non-main thread stack (#1101). Maintainers call this a configuration issue and advise 8 MiB thread stacks.

Jitter-entropy init can call abort(): #1072 (open) reports crashes in tree_jitter_initialize_once in Windows VMs, also seen in uv. The documented ~50 ms per-process cost does not appear in the wtx 1.4 ms whole-process runs, and the reason is not documented.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose it over ring or Graviola when you need FIPS, post-quantum KEM, extra primitives such as AES-CBC/CTR, CMAC or key wrap, or P-384-heavy handshakes. ring builds smaller and compiles faster, and ring and Graviola were faster with RSA-PSS certificates in wtx. Relative to the AWS-LC (C) and rustls entries, it is the Rust binding to AWS-LC and the crypto provider under rustls, not a competitor to them.
verified_claims_summary: c410-f3r's wtx-bench timed whole processes: decode 3 PEM files, run one loopback TLS handshake in WTX, and exit (hyperfine mean of 10 runs). Builds used the Rust deploy profile (opt-level 3, fat LTO, 1 codegen unit; rustc and OpenSSL versions unstated) on a Ryzen 9 5900X under Fedora. aws-lc-rs (vendored AWS-LC) took 1.38-6.71 ms against 4.41-10.20 ms for OpenSSL, 1.30-3.44x faster (median about 2.95x) in all 45 combinations. OpenSSL's near-constant penalty is unexplained by the author, so this is weak evidence about crypto speed.
status_note: Active and widely used: v1.18.1 (2026-09-01), last commit 2026-09-17, about 237M crates.io downloads (88.6M in the last 90 days) and 366 reverse dependencies, under Apache-2.0 or ISC. Security fixes ship through aws-lc-sys (five 2026 RustSec advisories, patched in >=0.38/0.39), so keep the sys crate current.
